## stella-core/src/loop_detect.rs
    1  //! Loop detection — pure synchronous analysis of recent tool calls and
    2  //! the results they produced: plain synchronous functions over owned
    3  //! data, easy to property-test, run by the step-driver alongside
    4  //! compaction and budget eviction.
    5  //!
    6  //! A flat iteration cap alone burns the *entire* step budget before
    7  //! giving up, even when the model got stuck after three steps. This
    8  //! module gives the step-driver (`driver.rs`, which every CLI path
    9  //! drives) a real, typed verdict it can act on early: steer or abort with

## stella-core/src/receipts.rs
    1  //! Context-receipts emission (spec §4/§5), kept out of the driver body so the
    2  //! step loop calls one helper and the emission logic stays independently
    3  //! testable. Produces, per step: a `BlockRegistered` event for each context
    4  //! block the model has not seen before (content-addressed, emitted once), then
    5  //! a `StepManifest` naming the blocks it saw this step in wire order.
    6  //!
    7  //! Content-free by construction: blocks carry a `content_digest`, never the
    8  //! payload bytes — the preimage already lives in the originating event in the
    9  //! journal, so this is an index over the fold, not a second content store.

## stella-tools/src/custom.rs
    1  //! `custom` — developer-defined **script tools**, discovered from the
    2  //! filesystem with zero registration ceremony.
    3  //!
    4  //! A developer gives the agent a new tool by dropping a TOML manifest next to
    5  //! a script. At CLI startup every manifest under `.stella/tools/` (workspace)
    6  //! and `~/.stella/tools/` (user-global) is discovered automatically and
    7  //! advertised to the model alongside the native tools ([`crate::registry`]).
    8  //! No flags, no registry edits — a bash script plus a ten-line manifest is a
    9  //! working agent tool. Rich or stateful integrations use an MCP server
